I hit the tool limit mid-investigation, so rather than hand you a half-verified archive, here's exactly where I got to and what I found. Two of these are things you'll want to know before the next delivery.

The dump is one commit stale
/mnt/project/dump.txt is at 825b817. Your repo is at 966bd1a, which includes M6 Slice 21 (CONTAINER_ENGINE engine selection in backup.sh/restore_drill.sh, the data-loaded barrier on CounterBoard.razor). I worked against a fresh clone instead, so nothing below is based on the stale copy.

Slice 21 left documentation debt
This is the one worth acting on first, because §18's atomic-documentation rule was broken by the delivery itself:

docs/_append/BUILD_PROGRESS-M6-Slice-21.md is committed and unmerged. docs/BUILD_PROGRESS.md still ends at Slice 20.
F-43 and F-44 appear nowhere in docs/DOCUMENTATION_REVIEW.md or docs/TECHNICAL_SPECIFICATION.md — not in Group E, not in Appendix A, no changelog entry. They exist only in that unmerged append file and one line of OPERATIONS.md §84.
Given what you've said about bespoke scripts, the fix is a full docs/BUILD_PROGRESS.md (existing + Slice 21 + the new slice) and docs/_append/BUILD_PROGRESS-M6-Slice-21.md in the delete list. No cat >> anywhere.

Two new findings, both measured
The build context is the whole working tree. There is no .dockerignore (or .containerignore) anywhere, and Containerfile line 27 is COPY . . with the repository root as context. Measured on a fresh clone: 31 MB, of which docs/llm/ is 16 MB and .git/ is 11 MB — 87% the build cannot use. Worse than slow: git-ignored is not context-ignored, so .env, .dataprotection/, and every *.dump / *-dataprotection.tar go into the build stage whenever they sit in the tree — and OPERATIONS §12 documents the upgrade as backup first, then up -d --build, which is precisely the order that puts the key ring §8 calls "the key material, in the clear" into the image builder. CI escapes only by accident of step ordering (docker build runs before backup.sh writes ci-backups/).

I verified the mechanics rather than assuming them: Docker/BuildKit reads .dockerignore at the context root (a Containerfile.dockerignore would take precedence, and won't exist); Podman reads .containerignore or .dockerignore, preferring the former if both exist. One root .dockerignore covers both engines. I'd planned an allow-list (* then explicit re-includes) plus an executable guard as a RUN in the build stage, so a deleted or renamed ignore file fails the build loudly on every machine instead of only in CI.

OPERATIONS.md:236 asserts a repository setting — F-42's rule, broken past the gate built to make it unrepeatable. The sentence is "The images are public, so no registry login is needed to pull." That is a claim about a GitHub Packages visibility checkbox, in the indicative, about a package that does not exist yet — and GitHub's own documentation contradicts itself on what the value will be (the Actions page says a GITHUB_TOKEN-published package inherits the repository's visibility; the packages page says it inherits permissions but not visibility). check_repository.sh gate 3 passes on your tree today because PLATFORM_STATE_CLAIMS only lists issues, pull requests, discussions and the wiki. I confirmed it's the only occurrence in the tree.

Repository state, for the record
Description set, private vulnerability reporting on — both Slice 20 operator actions are done. Zero tags, zero releases, latest ci run on main green. Every action version in release.yml resolves (docker/build-push-action@v7, metadata-action@v6, login-action@v4, setup-buildx-action@v4 all exist and are current majors), so the release path isn't broken at that layer. One thing I noticed but did not chase: release.yml's verify job calls ci.yml without secrets: inherit, so ADMIN_READ_TOKEN won't reach the governance job and its advisory half will silently skip on the one run that matters most.

Say the word and I'll build the archive: .dockerignore, Containerfile, scripts/check_repository.sh, docs/OPERATIONS.md, docs/TECHNICAL_SPECIFICATION.md (v1.7, Appendix A gaining F-43 through F-46), docs/DOCUMENTATION_REVIEW.md, the full docs/BUILD_PROGRESS.md, and _CHANGES.md — full files, exact paths, with docs/_append/BUILD_PROGRESS-M6-Slice-21.md as the single deletion.

M6 Slice 22 — what leaves this machine. Eleven full files, exact repo-relative paths, extracts at the repository root.

bash
tar -xzf m6-slice-22-build-context-and-package-visibility.tar.gz -C /home/kushal/src/dotnet/myrestaurant
cd /home/kushal/src/dotnet/myrestaurant
git rm docs/_append/BUILD_PROGRESS-M6-Slice-21.md
git add .dockerignore
Delete: docs/_append/BUILD_PROGRESS-M6-Slice-21.md — its contents are now inside docs/BUILD_PROGRESS.md, verified byte-identical. docs/_append/ goes with it; nothing will be delivered there again. Both git commands matter: every gate you have enumerates with git ls-files, so an untracked .dockerignore is unchecked by all of them and missing from the fresh clone CI builds from.

Slice 21's debt is closed. F-43 and F-44 were working code with no ledger row anywhere — not in BUILD_PROGRESS.md, not in Group E, not in Appendix A. Both are written now, dated to Slice 21.

F-45 — the build context was the whole working tree. No .dockerignore has ever existed here. Measured on a fresh clone: 458 files, 31,148,997 bytes, of which docs/llm/ is 16 MB and .git/ is 11 MB. The size is the harmless half. A build context is not a commit, so .gitignore — correct about .env, .dataprotection/ and every -dataprotection.tar — protected none of them; neither engine reads it. And OPERATIONS §12 documents the upgrade as backup, then up -d --build, so the documented procedure handed the key ring to the image builder. CI escaped by step ordering alone. The fix is an allow-list (169 files, 1.6 MB) plus a guard in Containerfile that fails the build unless the context is exactly that — running on your workstation, not only in CI, because yours is the machine with a key ring in the tree.

F-46 — the F-42 rule, enforced as a list of examples. Gate 3 landed green in Slice 20 and was already wrong: OPERATIONS §14 asserted a package visibility setting while the gate enumerated the repository page, about a package that didn't exist, and GitHub's own docs contradict themselves on which way that switch falls. Second half of the same blind spot: the advisory settings report never ran on a release, because release.yml passed the called workflow no secrets — so the one run that creates a package reported nothing about packages.

Worth running by hand, since no other gate touches the new file:

bash
podman build --file Containerfile --tag myrestaurant_web:local .
#  expect an early "build context accepted: 169 file(s)"
dotnet test should still read 996 / 0 failed — no C#, no Razor, no .csproj in this delivery. One honest gap: shellcheck wasn't available in the sandbox, so check_repository.sh got bash -n only; the change is two array literals and comment text, and CI runs shellcheck regardless.
